title: Classification and normalization of representing traces
statement: Let C and D be categories, F:C→D a functor, M an object of C, and U an object of D. Call t:F(M)→U representing when, for every K in C, the function a↦F(a)≫t from Hom(K,M) to Hom(F(K),U) is bijective. (1) If F⊣G and e:M≅G(U), then F(e.hom)≫ε_U is representing; it is the unique representing t whose adjunct is e.hom. (2) If t is representing, then t' is representing if and only if there exists a unique e:M≅M such that F(e.hom)≫t=t'. (3) Given one representing t, there is a unique representing trace if and only if every automorphism of M has hom equal to id_M. (4) Given equivalences E_K:Hom(K,M)≃Hom(F(K),U) satisfying E_K(a≫b)=F(a)≫E_L(b), there exists a unique representing t satisfying F(a)≫t=E_K(a) for all K and a; it is E_M(id_M). These assertions also hold for zero objects and arbitrary category and Hom universes.

proof.text: For a specified isomorphism e to the right-adjoint value, compose postcomposition by e.hom with the inverse adjunction equivalence. Its counit formula is the asserted Hom function, hence it is bijective. Injectivity of the adjunction equivalence proves uniqueness with the prescribed adjunct.
Precomposition by a source automorphism preserves each representing bijection, by composing it with a↦a≫e.hom, whose inverse is a↦a≫e.inv.

Represent t prime using t and t using t prime at K=M, obtaining a and b. Functoriality and the two representing injections imply a≫b=id and b≫a=id. This constructs an automorphism. Injectivity at M proves its uniqueness; the converse is the preceding step.

A unique trace makes every transformed trace equal to the original; its representing injection forces every automorphism to be identity. Conversely the classification and identity condition make every representing trace equal to the original.
For normalized E take t=E_M(id_M). Naturality with b=id gives its normalization and identifies every Hom function with E_K. Evaluation at id_M gives uniqueness.

theorem representingTrace_of_iso
    {G : D ⥤ C} (adj : F ⊣ G) (e : M ≅ G.obj U) :
    ∀ K : C, Function.Bijective
      (fun a : K ⟶ M ↦ F.map a ≫ F.map e.hom ≫ adj.counit.app U)

theorem existsUnique_trace_of_orientation
    {G : D ⥤ C} (adj : F ⊣ G) (e : M ≅ G.obj U) :
    ∃! t : F.obj M ⟶ U,
      (∀ K : C, Function.Bijective (fun a : K ⟶ M ↦ F.map a ≫ t)) ∧
      adj.homEquiv M U t = e.hom

theorem representingTrace_precompose_iso
    (t : F.obj M ⟶ U)
    (ht : ∀ K : C, Function.Bijective (fun a : K ⟶ M ↦ F.map a ≫ t))
    (e : M ≅ M) :
    ∀ K : C, Function.Bijective (fun a : K ⟶ M ↦ F.map a ≫ (F.map e.hom ≫ t))

theorem representingTrace_iff_existsUnique_iso
    (t : F.obj M ⟶ U)
    (ht : ∀ K : C, Function.Bijective (fun a : K ⟶ M ↦ F.map a ≫ t))
    (t' : F.obj M ⟶ U) :
    (∀ K : C, Function.Bijective (fun a : K ⟶ M ↦ F.map a ≫ t')) ↔
      ∃! e : M ≅ M, F.map e.hom ≫ t = t'

theorem existsUnique_representingTrace_iff
    (t : F.obj M ⟶ U)
    (ht : ∀ K : C, Function.Bijective (fun a : K ⟶ M ↦ F.map a ≫ t)) :
    (∃! t' : F.obj M ⟶ U,
      ∀ K : C, Function.Bijective (fun a : K ⟶ M ↦ F.map a ≫ t')) ↔
      ∀ e : M ≅ M, e.hom = 𝟙 M

theorem existsUnique_trace_of_normalized_pairing
    (E : ∀ K : C, (K ⟶ M) ≃ (F.obj K ⟶ U))
    (hE : ∀ (K L : C) (a : K ⟶ L) (b : L ⟶ M),
      E K (a ≫ b) = F.map a ≫ E L b) :
    ∃! t : F.obj M ⟶ U,
      (∀ K : C, Function.Bijective (fun a : K ⟶ M ↦ F.map a ≫ t)) ∧
      ∀ (K : C) (a : K ⟶ M), F.map a ≫ t = E K a
